newsitem.title: USA: Intel book-to-bill ratio greater than 1.0.
newsitem.headline: Intel book-to-bill ratio greater than 1.0.

text.p: Intel Corp said Tuesday its book-to-bill ratio -- a critical figure for estimating future demand for its computer chips -- was "greater than 1.0" in the second quarter.
Intel, which also reported second quarter earnings, did not specify an exact ratio.
The book-to-bill ratio measures the backlog of orders for products that a company has. A ratio of 1.01 means the company has orders for $101 of product for every $100 of goods shipped.
Intel said demand for its older Pentium chips dropped sharply, but that it has strong orders for the new Pentium II.
